newsitem.title: USA: AT&T Worldnet sees gains from AOL's woes.
newsitem.headline: AT&T Worldnet sees gains from AOL's woes.

text.p: AT&T Corp's head of its Worldnet Internet access service said AT&T has seen the number of its new subscribers double so far in the month of January, and many of its new subscribers are frustrated America Online Inc users.

Tom Evslin, vice president of AT&T Worldnet Service, said that after AT&T noticed a sudden increase in subscribers in recent weeks, it began interviewing new subscribers who were signing up to the service.
"We did a survey of people who are calling 1800 WorldNet and 44.5 percent of the 1,000 people we interviewed were AOL customers," he said.

Evslin said 77 percent of those AOL members said they were dissatisfied AOL users because of AOL's recent problems, as too many AOL users are clogging its network during peak hours and many users are not able to sign onto the service.

America Online Inc did not have any immediate comment. Last week, the world's largest online service said that it is spending more to upgrade its network, due to the sharp increase in usage since it switched its members to unlimited usage for a flat rate of $19.95 a month on December 1.
AT&T said it ended December with a total of 586,000 subscribers. It now has well over 600,000 subscribers.

Evslin would not disclose how many new subscribers joined AT&T Worldnet in January. He said AT&T has conducted a study of its service, with an outside research firm, and its results showed that AT&T has much more reliable service than its rivals.

When compared with nine other Internet service providers, AT&T said that the study showed AT&T users had a 94.4 percent chance of getting connected, during peak hours, versus an industry average of 90 percent. Peak hours refers to evening hours, starting at 6 p.m. until midnight, in each time zone.
According to a separate study by the same research firm which compared AT&T to AOL during peak hours, Worldnet had a 93.4 percent success rate, versus 36.7 percent for AOL.

"Seventy-seven percent (of those) were dissastified AOL customers," he said. The first study comparing AT&T and the Internet service providers was done from December 9 to December 23, AT&T said. The second study comparing AT&T and AOL was conducted for one week, from December 23 to January 2 and
"We designed our service for the price plan we are on," Evslin said, referring to AT&T's $19.95 a month flat rate pricing. AT&T is also running a new advertising campaign.
The telecommunications powerhouse will begin test marketing its ads this week, both television and print, which focus on the reliability of AT&T Worlnet.
"We will make a point about reliability and let people make their own conclusions," Evslin said, rather than target AOL's problems.

An AOL spokesman later said that AT&T is probably gaining from AOL's "bring your own access" new feature of its service, where users can access AOL for a lower cost via other Internet access providers. AT&T provides access to AOL via many high-speed T3 lines, through a joint deal of AT&T and AOL.
AOL also pointed out that AT&T subscribers base versus AOL's (which is currently at over eight million) is so small that their gains are "insignificant versus AOL."
